title: Disrupting a cargo receptor entrapment complex is a therapeutic node for distinct proteinopathies
title_zh: 破坏货物受体俘获复合体作为不同蛋白质病的治疗靶点
abstract: Toxic accumulation of mutant proteins within the secretory pathway contributes to genetically and clinically distinct proteinopathies, including inherited retinal disease. We identify a cargo receptor entrapment complex whose disruption clears accumulated mutant proteins and ameliorates disease phenotypes in the kidney and eye. The complex comprises transmembrane emp24 domain (TMED)7, TMED2, TMED9, and TMED10, and it retains structurally and functionally diverse mutant proteins in the early secretory pathway through TMED7 binding to the Golgi protein GRASP55. Disrupting this interaction-dependent entrapment mechanism promotes the clearance of accumulated cargoes. In vivo inducible genetic deletion of TMED7 or treatment with the small-molecule BRD7635 reverses histopathological hallmarks and rescues functional deficits across distinct proteinopathies, including mitigation of vision loss in a mouse model of retinitis pigmentosa. Together, these findings reveal a shared mechanism of mutant protein entrapment that can be therapeutically targeted across distinct diseases.
abstract_zh: 分泌通道中突变蛋白的有毒积累导致遗传和临床表型各异的蛋白质病，包括遗传性视网膜疾病。我们鉴定了一种货物受体俘获复合体，破坏该复合体可清除积累的突变蛋白并改善肾脏和眼部的疾病表型。该复合体由跨膜emp24域蛋白TMED7、TMED2、TMED9和TMED10组成，通过TMED7与高尔基体蛋白GRASP55结合，将结构和功能各异的突变蛋白滞留在早期分泌通道中。破坏这种依赖相互作用的俘获机制可促进积累货物的清除。在体诱导性TMED7基因缺失或使用小分子BRD7635可逆转不同蛋白质病的组织病理学特征并挽救功能缺陷，包括减轻视网膜色素变性小鼠模型中的视力丧失。这些发现共同揭示了一种可跨不同疾病进行治疗靶向的突变蛋白俘获共同机制。
